correctness.rationale: For a diagonal evaluation point, the right-evaluated entry in row \(i\), column \(j\) depends only on the scalar entry polynomial in that position evaluated at the \(j\)-th diagonal coordinate. This identifies the null ideal exactly as a column-wise divisibility module. Right multiplication by matrix units shows that two-sidedness forces every column divisor to divide every other one, hence all monic divisors agree. The converse is immediate because a common column divisor gives the matrix ideal \(M_n(hF[x])\). The finite-field count is ordinary inclusion-exclusion on missing coordinate-symbol pairs, and the asymptotic bound is a direct union bound. The packaged exhaustive checks agree with the formula in five complete finite cases.

originality.rationale: The 2022 primary source poses the general core-set problem and gives a complete algorithm only in dimension two. The 2022 three-dimensional sequel studies subsets of one irreducible similarity class, and the 2024 counting paper studies exact and asymptotic counts in the full \(2	imes2\) matrix ring. value.rationale: The theorem gives a complete all-dimensions solution on a natural semisimple commutative subalgebra in a problem whose general higher-dimensional form is described as difficult. It identifies the full null ideal, not only a yes/no criterion, and converts core-ness into a transparent combinatorial condition on coordinate projections. Over finite fields it yields both an exact count and a sharp elementary asymptotic lower bound, directly complementing the recent program of counting core sets.
